model: Stop location, accompanying stops: multinomial logit over 1,588 zones, sequential anchors, location mixture (article table est_stop_ACCOMPANY_stop)
purpose: Re-estimate the location choice of accompanying stops on tours and check it against the article.
depends_on: 14_tour_mode_work, 16_tour_mode_shopping, 17_tour_mode_other (and 15_tour_mode_school): the variable ls is the log-sum of the re-estimated tour mode models, read from 00_shared_data/mode_choice_logsums/m08_coef.csv (work, shopping, other; m09_coef.csv for school). The provided Biogeme data already contains ls at the published mode coefficients; re-estimated mode coefficients require rebuilding the ls data (step 2) with the new m08_coef.csv.

steps.what: optional (data already provided in input/data/estimation and input/data/holdout): estimation tables of the stops from the raw TAZ record files
optional (data already provided): wide Biogeme data: detour and mode-choice logsum of every anchor configuration to every zone
check: log-likelihood at the article estimates, without estimating (writes nothing)

steps.memory_gb: see notes (expected beyond the free memory of this machine)

check.basis: full estimation half, all 3515 records (eager evaluation, rows grouped by number of anchor configurations); project likelihood -12417.4835 (full precision) / -12417.4835 (article)

notes: Steps 1-2 need the project Python with numpy, pandas, pyarrow and torch (python3); the Biogeme venv has no torch. Their output is already in input/data.
Full choice set of 1,588 zones, no sampling of alternatives; location mixture over up to 4 anchor configurations and up to 4 possible zones of the stop (padding configurations / zones have weight 0).
Size term: base school pupils; components population, retail, office and other jobs; MU_size estimated (0.920). Bounds: THETA in [-30, 15], MU_size in [0, 3].
Detour pieces start at 1 km where the article has no 0-1 km piece (slope 0 below 1 km); the top piece is detour above 20 km.
ls (mode-choice logsum of the detour) comes from the tour mode models (00_shared_data/mode_choice_logsums/m08_coef.csv).

Estimation memory: Measured (shopping stops, Biogeme 3.3.5 default JIT): compiling and evaluating the log-likelihood, its gradient and the BHHH matrix on 20 records with ONE anchor configuration took 29 min and 6.1 GB peak memory (compile dominated; the machine was under memory pressure). The estimation expression has up to 4 configurations (4 x 1,588 utilities plus the candidate zones, about 4 times larger), so compiling alone is expected to need about 25 GB or more and several hours, and the reverse-mode intermediates at run time about (expression nodes x records x 8 bytes), i.e. roughly 10-30 GB more (4,000-8,000 records); with the default analytical Hessian more again. Expected total: about 30-50 GB. This does not fit on this machine (48 GB, about 45 GB used by other jobs): the exact full-set mixture estimation in Biogeme is infeasible here and was not run. It needs a machine with about 64 GB free; in biogeme.toml set calculating_second_derivatives = "never" (BHHH) or analytical_hessian_mode = "chunked" to limit the Hessian. The likelihood is not changed or approximated. The evaluation at given coefficients (--evaluate, use_jit=False) needs under 2 GB.
